nodes.description: A patent document titled "Real-time ad-hoc spam filtering of email" describing a multi-pass ad-hoc spam message filtering approach.

A filtering approach that dynamically generates a temporary classifier during a first pass based on results of a previously applied message filter that sorts messages into folders, then uses the classifier in a second pass to retrospectively inspect messages.

A model generated during the first pass analysis based on message folder placement and message attributes, used to score and identify misclassified messages; it resides exclusively in non-persistent memory and is purged after use.

A message filter configured to sort messages into different message folders and store first classification data in a persistent store; it may execute on a network device distinct from a client device.<SEP>A previously applied message filter that sorts messages into a plurality of different message folders and stores first classification data in a persistent store.<SEP>A message filter configured to sort messages into different message folders and to store first classification data in a persistent store.

A filter configured to generate a classification model based on a first pass analysis, perform a second pass on sorted messages to identify misclassifications, and purge the model from non-persistent memory.

A device distinct from a client device on which the first message filter is configured to execute.<SEP>A device comprising a transceiver to send and receive data over a network and a processor operative to perform first and second pass analyses, display misclassification identifications, and purge the classification model from non-persistent memory.<SEP>A device configured to receive messages, assign them to message folders using the first message filter, and communicate the messages over a network to the message folders.
A component of the network device that sends and receives data over a network.
A component of the network device operative to perform actions including first pass analysis, second pass analysis, displaying misclassification identifications, and purging the classification model.

A plurality of different folders into which messages are sorted by the first message filter, used as a basis for training and generating the classification model.<SEP>Different folders into which messages are sorted by the first message filter and to which identified messages may be moved by a user.
A generated identification of sorted messages that might be misclassified, displayed so that at least one misclassified message can be moved to a different message folder.
A memory-resident-only location where the generated classification model resides exclusively, not stored on disk or in another persistent data store, and from which the model is purged.
A storage location where the first message filter stores first classification data.<SEP>A data store where the first message filter stores first classification data.

A storage medium readable by a processor that stores instructions for executing the multi-pass message filter and related operations.<SEP>A medium including data and instructions whose execution on a computing device provides for managing messages.

A device on which the first and second passes of the multi-pass message filter may execute entirely, and on which the first pass is executed to train the multi-pass message filter.<SEP>A user's device on which the classification model is maintained in memory and on which the first and second passes of the multi-pass message filter may occur entirely.<SEP>A device that executes the passes of the multi-pass message filter, generates second classification data in non-persistent memory, scores messages, identifies mis-sorted messages, and provides a display of information enabling a user to move messages.

A book associated with a recipient that is associated with the message folders, used in analysis to determine whether a message sender's address is present.<SEP>An address book associated with a recipient that is associated with the message folders, whose sender addresses may be analyzed to generate second classification data.
A header of a message, including a subject and originating network address, read during the first pass analysis.<SEP>A header of a message that may be analyzed to generate second classification data.

The contents of a message read during the first pass analysis and used in generating the classification model.<SEP>The content of a message that may be analyzed to generate second classification data.
Attachments of messages read during the first pass analysis.
Information about the sender of a message, read during the first pass analysis.

A score assigned to each message during the second pass using the second classification data, used to identify messages sorted into an incorrect message folder.<SEP>A score assigned to each message by the second pass of the multi-pass message filter, used to indicate whether a message is sorted into an incorrect message folder.

A message filtering method that executes in multiple passes, including a first pass on a client device to train the filter by generating second classification data, and employs a Naive Bayes classifier.<SEP>A message filter executed in multiple passes on a client device; a first pass trains the filter by generating second classification data, and a second pass scores each message to identify mis-sorted messages.
A classifier employed by the multi-pass message filter for classifying messages.
Data stored in a persistent store by the first message filter.<SEP>Classification data generated by the first message filter and stored in a persistent store.

Data generated during the first pass of the multi-pass message filter to train the filter, and which can be deleted such that it is no longer accessible.<SEP>Classification data generated during the first pass of the multi-pass message filter, configured to reside exclusively in a non-persistent memory store and deleted from the client device upon providing the display of information.
A model generated based on an analysis of at least which message folder a message currently resides.
One of a plurality of different folders into which messages are sorted, and whose current residence of a message is analyzed to generate the second classification model.

A method for managing message delivery comprising receiving messages, sorting them into folders using a first message filter, and executing a first pass of a multi-pass message filter on a client device.<SEP>A method for managing message delivery that involves receiving messages, sorting them into folders using a first message filter, and executing a multi-pass message filter on a client device to identify messages sorted into incorrect folders.
A memory store at the client device where the second classification data resides exclusively.
A message received and sorted into message folders, scored by the multi-pass message filter, and potentially identified as stored in an incorrect folder.
A message folder into which a message has been incorrectly sorted, as indicated by the message's score.
A person enabled to move an identified message to another message folder and able to select execution of the multi-pass message filter through an interface on the client device.
An interface on the client device through which a user can select execution of the multi-pass message filter.
A network over which the network device communicates messages to the message folders.
A system for enabling communications over a network, comprising a network device and a client device.
A state of a message that may be analyzed to generate second classification data.
